Subject: BlueNova — postmortem packet (shared ahead of Wed readout)

Ian / BlueNova team,

Attached is the customer-facing postmortem packet for the Dec 18 service irregularity. High-level summary up front:

Impact: short-lived increase in token latency and intermittent 502s on your dedicated inference pool impacting ~12% of requests between 2026-12-18 03:42:00 UTC and 2026-12-18 04:21:00 UTC. No request bodies or customer payloads were exfiltrated.

Root cause (condensed): a cascade of events started with an autoscaler mis-evaluation when a transient scheduler metric spike caused several GPU instances to be drained and reattached simultaneously to the Dedicated pool used by BlueNova. This coincided with a rare kernel selection edge case in our runtime where a long-tail sequence length distribution caused increased memory pressure and KV-cache eviction churn. The combination caused increased latency and then transient 502 errors when the runtime failed to rehydrate the KV cache quickly for warm sessions.

Evidence and what we validated:
- Request traces (trace ids included) showing successful replays of affected requests — no payload leakage detected.
- Replay verification against your pinned model version showing identical outputs pre/post-incident.
- Checksums for attached artifacts (see evidence_bundle_checksums.txt).

Immediate mitigations applied (same day):
1) Emergency autoscaler rule tightened to prevent concurrent drain of >25% of nodes in a pool.
2) Runtime patch deployed to bypass the problematic kernel selection path for sequences >6k tokens and fall back to the stable kernel.
3) KV cache warm-up tweak to prefer prefix prefetch for pinned sessions.

Planned next steps (owner / ETA):
- Karthik: full autoscaler policy review + regression test (ETA 2027-01-07) — Jira OPS-4981.
- Platform: additional runtime integration tests for kernel selection with variable sequence distributions (ETA 2027-01-14).
- Neha/Evelyn: provide verification run and evidence package to BlueNova for audit (ETA 2026-12-27).

Attachments included: bluenova_postmortem_summary.pdf (this packet), bluenova_timeline.csv (detailed event timeline with traces), evidence_bundle_checksums.txt (SHA256 sums for artifacts). All artifacts are accessible from the Drive link below.

Short answer to your compliance question: no customer PII was written to any central debugging logs and no artifacts created during the incident contain unredacted customer data. We verify this in the attached evidence bundle and checksum manifest. If your security team would like, we can run a joint verification of the artifacts during our readout.

Link to artifacts: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2B_BlueNova_Postmortem
Jira (internal): https://redwood-inference.atlassian.net/browse/OPS-4981

I’ll present this packet at Wed 12/23 14:30 PT and Karthik will cover the technical mitigations and timelines. Evelyn will review the verification and compliance steps.

Neha

Ian — quick technical clarifications from the readout we ran:

- The kernel-selection edge case only activated when three conditions met: transient scheduler spike, >25% concurrent node drain, and median sequence length > 3k with a heavy tail. We reproduced locally and have a unit test now.
- Mitigation details: the runtime patch enforces a deterministic kernel selection for sequence buckets and adds a fall-back timer to avoid extended stalls. That change is non-destructive and will be part of the next full runtime release (canary ETA 2027-01-10).
- Autoscaler policy: we've added an explicit guardrail and a chaos-test in CI to prevent future correlated drains.

Action items for BlueNova verification (what we will hand over):
1) Replay package (contained in the Drive folder) with request traces and the exact model binary checksums.
2) Runbook excerpt describing how to validate there was no PII in artifacts (we redacted token-level debug dumps).
3) Weekly verification cadence proposal for the first 3 weeks after the patch (we suggest Fri checks for the first 3 releases).

If your ops team wants, we can open a temporary read-only S3 bucket with the replay artifacts for a period of 30 days; confirm and we’ll provision.

Karthik
Principal Platform Engineer | Redwood Inference
